title: Testing 38 questions against expected results
changed: Ten SQL questions that depend on how each owner defines a term. A 'regular' at Mekong Noodle House has three or more completed orders in three months; at Ridgeline Coffee, four or more orders in a month. General definitions are in [the prompt](https://github.com/rostgoat/restaurant-ops-agent/blob/main/api/app/agent/prompt.py). Each restaurant's definitions are in a document the agent can search alongside its policies.
I wrote a reference query for each SQL question to calculate the expected answer.

Fifteen policy questions, including two where the closest search result does not answer the question. Eight action proposals to check against the rules. Three requests the agent should decline, one question about another restaurant's data, and one it can answer without searching.
Twenty-four months of test data, including menus, food costs, prices by sales channel, a promotion, loyalty rewards, seasonal items, and regular customers who stop ordering.
The policy search uses a similarity threshold of 0.50. I chose it after inspecting ten earlier runs.
moved: [sql-05](/evaluation/sql-05) was wrong by 6%. The query passed the safety checks but used the wrong time zone conversion.
[pol-02](/evaluation/pol-02) and [pol-12](/evaluation/pol-12) failed because the relevant sections scored 0.28 and 0.47, below the search threshold.
[pol-11](/evaluation/pol-11) answered correctly but shortened a citation label, which the citation check rejected.
next: Lower the search threshold from 0.50 to 0.40.

title: Lowering the search threshold to 0.40
changed: I lowered the minimum similarity score for showing a policy section from 0.50 to 0.40. The questions, expected answers, model, and prompt stayed the same.
moved: [pol-12](/evaluation/pol-12) passed.
[pol-05](/evaluation/pol-05) failed. The agent cited a related section to explain that it did not apply, which the grader treated as an error.
[pol-03](/evaluation/pol-03) failed because it shortened a citation label, as pol-11 had in the first run.
[sql-05](/evaluation/sql-05), [pol-02](/evaluation/pol-02), and [pol-11](/evaluation/pol-11) still failed. Retrieval recall rose from 86% to 93%; precision fell from 46% to 29%.
next: Keep the lower threshold and add instructions for date boundaries to address sql-05.

title: Adding time zone instructions to the prompt
changed: I added five lines to [the prompt](https://github.com/rostgoat/restaurant-ops-agent/blob/main/api/app/agent/prompt.py) explaining how to convert date boundaries into the restaurant's time zone. The instructions specify timestamp literals rather than timestamptz literals, which convert in the opposite direction. The questions, expected answers, model, and search threshold stayed the same.
Before the full run, I tested the failing case three times on its own. It passed all three times.
moved: [sql-05](/evaluation/sql-05) passed.
[pol-03](/evaluation/pol-03) passed, but [pol-11](/evaluation/pol-11) failed again. The agent still sometimes shortened citation labels.
[pol-02](/evaluation/pol-02) and [pol-05](/evaluation/pol-05) still failed.
next: Tell the agent to use full citation labels.

title: Requiring full citation labels
changed: I added two sentences to [the prompt](https://github.com/rostgoat/restaurant-ops-agent/blob/main/api/app/agent/prompt.py) requiring the full citation label every time, including repeated citations. Short forms such as [§2] and [House Policy §2] are not accepted. Nothing else changed.
Before the full run, I tested each of the two affected cases three times. All six answers passed the citation check.
moved: [pol-11](/evaluation/pol-11) passed. No answer in the run used a shortened citation label.
[pol-02](/evaluation/pol-02) passed after the agent used different search wording. The relevant section scored 0.51, above the threshold, but the search problem remained unresolved.
[pol-05](/evaluation/pol-05) still failed.
next: Review how the grader handles questions the policies do not cover.

title: Correcting the grader for questions outside the policies
changed: I removed two rules from [the grader](https://github.com/rostgoat/restaurant-ops-agent/blob/main/api/app/evals/grade.py). A question outside the policies used to fail if the agent retrieved or cited any section. It now passes if the answer says the policies do not cover the question and does not present a citation as an applicable rule. The citation check also applies to every policy case.

With this grading change, run 2 would score 34 and run 4 would score 38. Run 3 would still score 35: its answer said it couldn't find a rule, but the grader's accepted phrases did not include that wording.
moved: [pol-05](/evaluation/pol-05) passed, though this run did not test the grading change. The related section scored 0.38, below the 0.40 threshold, so the agent never saw or cited it.
[pol-02](/evaluation/pol-02) failed again. Across three searches, the relevant section's best score was 0.36. The answer had no citation.
[pol-11](/evaluation/pol-11) failed because the answer addressed the owner as 'you', while the grader required the word 'owner'. All citation labels were complete.
next: Add accepted phrases for 'couldn't find' and for answers that address the owner as 'you'.

title: Regrading earlier answers with more accepted phrases
changed: I expanded two phrase lists in [the test cases](https://github.com/rostgoat/restaurant-ops-agent/blob/main/api/evals/cases.json). The health inspection case now accepts 'couldn't find' and 'could not find'. The campaign case accepts 'you approve', 'you can approve', and 'your approval', since the person asking is the owner.
I regraded the five saved runs using these phrases and the grading change from run 5. I did not call the model again.
result: After regrading: run 2 passed 34, run 3 passed 36, run 4 passed 38, and run 5 passed 37.
moved: [pol-05](/evaluation/pol-05) passed in runs 2, 3, and 4. Those answers either used wording the grader had not accepted or cited a related section to explain that it did not apply.
[pol-11](/evaluation/pol-11) passed in run 5. Its answer said 'unless you approve more', correctly referring to the owner.
[pol-02](/evaluation/pol-02) still failed in every run except run 4. Expanding the phrase lists corrected grading errors; it did not fix the search that hid the relevant section.
next: Add keyword matching to policy search. I had tried prompt changes six times on the failing case, but the relevant section still scored between 0.37 and 0.39, below the 0.40 threshold.

title: Adding keyword matching to policy search
changed: [Policy search](https://github.com/rostgoat/restaurant-ops-agent/blob/main/api/app/policies/search.py) now ranks sections by both embedding similarity and matching words. Rare words receive more weight: 'DoorDash' in one of 25 sections counts more than 'order' in 15. The search combines the rankings and always includes the best keyword match, even if its similarity score is below the threshold. Postgres builds the keyword index from each section's text in a new table column.
I added tests for the search changes. The threshold, prompt, and grader stayed the same.
Before the full run, I tested the failing case three times with keyword matching. It passed all three, compared with one of six attempts using prompt changes alone.
moved: [pol-02](/evaluation/pol-02) passed. The first search returned the Delivery Marketplaces section through keyword matching, despite a similarity score of 0.34. The agent cited it.

Recall rose from 93% to 100%; precision fell from 29% to 28%. The agent saw 50 sections across 38 searches, compared with 45 sections in run 5. Five appeared through keyword matching alone: the previously missed section and, on four searches, the House Policy introduction. The agent ignored the introduction each time.
All other test outcomes stayed the same.
next: All 38 tests pass. Try a different model or add questions to test behavior this set does not cover.

title: Adding a question about catering orders
changed: I added sql-11, asking how many catering orders the restaurant had in October. A catering order contains an item from the menu's Catering category; the order itself has no catering channel, label, or discount. I found this case while trying questions the agent could reasonably interpret in more than one way, after it passed all 38 existing tests.
The prompt, search, threshold, and grader stayed the same so I could test the new question before making any fixes.
moved: [sql-11](/evaluation/sql-11) failed, as it had in three earlier manual tests. The agent searched order source labels and discount names for 'catering', found nothing, and said the data could not identify catering orders. It did not check the menu categories, although the prompt describes them.
All other test outcomes stayed the same.
next: Address answers that treat an empty query result as proof the data cannot answer the question. I had seen this twice: for catering orders and for a day with no data.

title: Checking menu categories and correcting the catering test dates
changed: I added four lines to [the prompt](https://github.com/rostgoat/restaurant-ops-agent/blob/main/api/app/agent/prompt.py) telling the agent to check menu categories and items when a question names something it cannot find elsewhere. The instructions also explain that an empty search only shows that the word was absent from the fields searched.

I corrected the test question too. It asked about October, but the test clock is fixed at October 24. The agent correctly counted through the 24th, while my reference query counted through the end of the data. The question now asks about September, a complete month with 22 catering orders.

Before the full run, I tested the September question three times with and without the new instructions. Without them, the agent found the menu category twice; with them, all three times. In the previous day's tests using the October question, it had found the category zero times out of three.
moved: [sql-11](/evaluation/sql-11) passed. The agent first listed the six items in the Catering category, then counted completed September orders containing at least one of them.
All other test outcomes stayed the same. Retrieval precision rose from 28% to 30%.
next: The full run included both a prompt change and a corrected question, so it cannot establish how much the prompt helped. The separate tests provide some evidence. I also still need an example where the agent cites a section that does not support its answer, the third type of error described on the home page.

title: Testing Haiku 5.5 on the same 39 questions
changed: I switched from Sonnet 5.5 to Haiku 5.5 at the same reasoning effort. The prompt, search threshold, and grader stayed the same.

Before this run, I manually tested Sonnet with 34 questions designed to make it cite a section for a rule that was not there. These covered sections with a different figure, sections silent on a specific situation, references to another document, and references to outside law. None produced that error.
moved: [pol-15](/evaluation/pol-15) failed because the answer said "don't include", while the grader only accepted "not include" and "doesn't include".
[pro-04](/evaluation/pro-04) failed because Haiku asked the owner to check for a packing photo instead of proposing a dispute. The action checker therefore received no proposal.
All other test outcomes stayed the same. Haiku cost about one-twelfth as much, with similar response times. No answer used Markdown formatting.
next: I need to add the missing phrase to the grader and decide which model the agent will use. Then I will run the tests once more on that model with nothing else changed.

title: Closing run: Sonnet 5.5 on the same 39 questions again
changed: I added "don't include" and "do not include" to the accepted phrases for the hospital staff question. With that change, run 9 regrades to 38 of 39.

I decided to keep Sonnet 5.5. Haiku did not propose the Uber Eats dispute, and proposing actions for the checker to evaluate is the agent's most important function. The Architecture page records this decision.
Nothing else changed. This run repeats run 8 to confirm that the 39 of 39 result holds a second time on the same model.
moved: All test outcomes stayed the same. Every test passed, including the two that Haiku failed. Retrieval precision was 30% and recall 100%, matching run 8.
next: This closes the experiment. Every failure across ten runs is documented on this page, and each of the three error types from the home page has a recorded result.
